rationale: PMID32249637 reports a whole-diet MS fatigue comparison. The original full outcome model and the processing and consumption details for canola remain unresolved. Available endpoint summaries do not agree on the strength of the difference.

The TRIHEP3 Huntington trial uses safflower oil as comparator and provides the aggregate PBA-s result. The apathy-item result and supplement details remain unavailable. Oil processing and an oil-free control are unverified.

The clove product-name match does not establish culinary clove. Registry NCT06295822 concerns a compound topical oil for menstrual pain. Earlier essential-oil and other mixtures have no ground-clove daytime sleepiness comparison in Parkinson disease.
Zucchini in the editorial is an author surname. The reviewed diet and allergy sources supply no isolated raw zucchini and dream enactment measure.

The Russian publisher original reports better olfaction for the thyme-containing adjunct in acute rhinosinusitis, with neurodegenerative disease excluded. The constituents were not isolated. Prospective scent-training and oil mixture registrations supply no ingested fresh-thyme Parkinson comparison.

The animal literature on isolated carvone measures anesthetic sleep duration, not REM dream enactment. The final source mentions either a company or researcher named Caraway rather than an assigned ingredient.
The 1995 conference was checked in full. A separate ingredient-focused overlay still records 456 pending appearances and original meal methods and processing in PMID7939393 remain unverified.

The mixed fermented red-cabbage, beet and caraway comparison reports inconclusive depression results. The original processing and constituent reports do not isolate the frozen cooked cabbage or measure Parkinson depression.

The soybean-oil emulsion report concerns intravenous nutrition in a different disease, without an attributable post-exposure dystonia result. The exact source review supplies no oral soybean-oil Parkinson comparison.

The original pain-domain table and processing grade for Khalil DOI 10.21608/aimj.2025.446526 remain unavailable. Completed NCT06944392 has no posted urinary or composite pain results and no controlled Parkinson comparison.

The poster concerns a coconut-associated fatty acid in experimental colitis. The reported Parkinson MCT study found no clear overall sleepiness effect across its phases and did not assign virgin coconut oil.
The 1910 original gives no cayenne falls comparison. Clinical reports about chili-associated syncope do not measure Parkinson fall frequency, including one episode that occurred while seated.
The original medication review supplies no tofu comparison. Acute okara effects on saliva and soft-tofu swallowing reports do not measure baked tofu and Parkinson drooling.

Fresh basil occurs within mixed menus and isolated extracts occur in preclinical work. The complete scopes and existing clinical sources contain no isolated fresh-basil estimate for Parkinson postural instability.
Dietary sunflower oil appears in a Parkinson composite symptom result and as a nonclinical vehicle. These contexts supply no isolated cold-pressed sunflower-oil estimate for dystonia.

The Churihar 2022 isolated cinnamaldehyde catalepsy original remains unverified. A later full article reports its result as null. This is a distinct compound and endpoint. The existing Maybe False score stays 50.005.

The original Bian abstract confirms six groups of ten, including positive control and vehicle. Full methods, voucher and direct dry-fried versus raw fraction comparison remain unavailable. NCT07562672 has no posted results and uses a topical mixture. The existing Maybe True score stays 50.005.
